questions.question: If 15 kg of sugar cost ₹600, what is the cost of 25 kg of sugar?
questions.questionHtml: If 15 kg of sugar cost ₹600, what is the cost of 25 kg of sugar?
questions.solution:
Cost of 1kg sugar (in Rs) = \(\frac{600}{15}= 40\)

The cost of 25 kg of sugar is 40 × 25 = Rs. 1000

questions.question: A man sold a radio set and gained one-eighth of its cost price. What is the profit percent?
questions.questionHtml: A man sold a radio set and gained one-eighth of its cost price. What is the profit percent?
questions.solution:
Given:

Profit = One-eighth of cost price

Concept Used:

Profit Percentage = \(\frac{Profit}{CP}× 100\)

Calculation:

Let the cost price of a radio set be Rs 100

Profit on selling radio set = \(\frac{1}{8}\) × 100 = 12.5 Rs

Profit Percentage =  \(\frac{12.5}{100}\) × 100 = 12.5 

∴ The profit percentage made on selling the radio set is 12.5%.

questions.question: Sohan purchased an old scooter, and sold it for Rs. 28,000 thus gaining a 12% profit on the cost price. The cost price of the scooter is:
questions.questionHtml: Sohan purchased an old scooter, and sold it for Rs. 28,000 thus gaining a 12% profit on the cost price. The cost price of the scooter is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The selling price of the scooter is Rs.28000.

The profit% is 12%.

Formula Used:

CP = 100/(100 + profit%) × SP 

Calculation:

The selling price of the scooter is Rs.28000.

The profit% is 12%.

The CP = 100/(100 + 12) × 28000

⇒ CP = 100/112 × 28000 = 25000

∴ The Cost price of the scooter is Rs.25000.

questions.question: 40% of the cost price of an article is equal to 30% of its selling price. The approximate percentage of profit or loss on the cost price is:
questions.questionHtml: 40% of the cost price of an article is equal to 30% of its selling price. The approximate percentage of profit or loss on the cost price is:
questions.solution:
40% Cost price = 30% selling price

4C = 3S ⇒ S = 4C/3

Profit % % = \(\frac{S-C}{C}\times 100 \) = \(\frac{\frac{4C}{3}-C}{C}\times 100\) = \(\frac{4-3}{3}\times 100\) = 33.33%

questions.question: A trader sells an article for Rs. 425 and loses 15%. At what price (in Rs.) should he sell the article to earn 5% profit?
questions.questionHtml: A trader sells an article for Rs. 425 and loses 15%. At what price (in Rs.) should he sell the article to earn 5% profit?
questions.solution:
The cost price of the article = 100/(100 - 15) × 425 ⇒ (100/85) × 425 ⇒  Rs. 500

The required selling price = (100 + 5)/100 × 500 ⇒ (105/100) × 500 ⇒ Rs. 525

questions.question: If the cost price of 70 articles is equal to the selling price of 40 articles, what will be the profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: If the cost price of 70 articles is equal to the selling price of 40 articles, what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
CP x 70 = SP x 40 ⇒ \(\frac{CP}{SP}=\frac{4}{7}\)

Let CP = Rs.4 and SP = Rs.7, then ⇒ Profit = SP - CP = 7 - 4 = Rs. 3

Profit% \(=\frac{profit}{costprice}× 100=\frac{3}{4}× 100\) = 3 × 25 = 75

questions.question: Salma buys an article and then sells if for Rs. 810. If she loses 10%, then at what price should she sell it to gain 4%?
questions.questionHtml: Salma buys an article and then sells if for Rs. 810. If she loses 10%, then at what price should she sell it to gain 4%?
questions.solution:
Given:

At loss 10%, SP of article = Rs. 810

Formula Used:

SP = CP × (1 + P%/100)

SP = CP × (1 – L%/100)

where, SP → Selling Price, CP → Cost Price

Calculations:

At loss 10%, SP of article = Rs. 810

Now, SP = CP × (1 – L%/100)

⇒ 810 = CP × (1 – 10/100)

⇒ 810 = CP × (9/10)      ----(1)

At gain 4%, 

SP = CP × (1 + 4/100)

⇒ SP = CP × (26/25)      ----(2)

Dividing (2) by (1), we get

⇒ SP/810 = [CP × (26/25)]/[CP × (9/10)]

⇒ SP/810 = 104/9

⇒ SP = (104/90) × 810

⇒ SP = Rs. 936

∴ The price at which Salma sells it to gain 4% is Rs. 936.

questions.question: P sells a mobile to Q at 10% loss and Q sells it to R at 25% profit. If R bought a mobile for Rs 45,000, then what was the cost price of the mobile for P?
questions.questionHtml: P sells a mobile to Q at 10% loss and Q sells it to R at 25% profit. If R bought a mobile for Rs 45,000, then what was the cost price of the mobile for P?
questions.solution:
Given:

SP(Q) = 45,000

P%(Q) = 25%

L%(P) = 10%

Formula used:

Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100
Loss% = (Loss / Cost Price) x 100
Profit = SP - CP
Loss = CP - SP
CP = Cost price
SP = Selling price

Solution:

For profit% of Q,

25 = [45000/CP - 1] x 100

0.25 + 1 = 45000/CP

CP = 45000/1.25 = 36000

Now, the CP of Q = SP of P

Hence, for loss% of P

10% = [1 - 36000/CP] x 100

0.1 - 1 = - 36000/CP

CP = 36000/0.9 = 40,000

Hence, the orignal cost price for P = Rs. 40,000.

questions.question: A person buys a table fan for Rs. 1,800 and sells it at a loss of 25%. What is the selling price of the table fan?
questions.questionHtml: A person buys a table fan for Rs. 1,800 and sells it at a loss of 25%. What is the selling price of the table fan?
questions.solution:
Given:

CP of table fan= Rs. 1800

Loss%= 25%

Formula Used:

Loss%=\(\frac{CP-SP}{CP}\times 100\)

Calculations:

According to the formula,

⇒ Loss%=\(\frac{CP-SP}{CP}\times 100\)

⇒ 25=\(\frac{1800-SP}{1800}\times 100\)

⇒ 25=\(\frac{1800-SP}{18}\)

⇒ 450= 1800 - SP

⇒ SP= 1800 - 450 = 1350

Hence, The selling price of the article is Rs. 1350

questions.question: The cost price of 10 goods is equal to the selling price of 8 goods. Find the profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: The cost price of 10 goods is equal to the selling price of 8 goods. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Given:

CP of 10 = SP of 8

Concept used:

Profit (in %) = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

Calculation:

Let, CP of 10 = 100 units

So, CP of 1 = 100/10 = 10 units

Also, SP of 8 = 100 units

So, SP of 1 = 100/8 = 12.5 units

% Profit = (12.5 - 10)/10 × 100

⇒ 2.5/10 × 100 = 2.5 × 10 = 25%

∴ The profit percentage is 25%.

Shortcut Trick 

Profit percentage = (10 - 8)/8 × 100

⇒ 2/8 × 100 = 25%

∴ The profit percentage is 25%.

questions.question: If the selling price of 50 articles is equal to the cost price of 42 articles, the what is the approximate loss or profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: If the selling price of 50 articles is equal to the cost price of 42 articles, the what is the approximate loss or profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

Article purchased = 42

Article sold = 50

Formula used:

Profit% or Loss% = [(the difference between S.P and CP.)/C.P]/100

If S.P is more than C.P then it is profit 

If C.P is more than S.P then it is Loss

Calculation:

Let the C.P of one article be x 

and the S.P of one article be y

C.P for the 42 articles will be = 42x

S.P for the 50 articles will be = 50y

Now according to the question

⇒ C.P = S.P

⇒ 42x = 50y

⇒ x : y =50 : 42 ⇒ 25 : 21

Here C.P is 25 and S.P is 21. so, C.P is greater than S.P which means loss

Loss = C.P - S.P = 25 - 21 = 4

Loss% = (4/25) × 100 = 4 × 4 = 16%

∴ The loss% is 16%

  

We can deal in articles also

Formula Used:

Profit% or Loss% = (d/sold article) × 100

where d = difference between the no. article sold and bought

Loss = no. of articles sold is more than bought

Profit = no. of articles brought is more than sold

Calculation:

d = 50 - 42 =8

Loss% = (8/50)× 100 = 16%

∴ The loss% is 16%.

questions.question: If an article is sold for Rs. 402, there is a loss of 33%. At what price should it be sold to get 37% profit?
questions.questionHtml: If an article is sold for Rs. 402, there is a loss of 33%. At what price should it be sold to get 37% profit?
questions.solution:
Given:

That the article is sold for Rs. 402 at a loss of 33%

Formula used:

Cost Price - Loss = Selling Price

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit

calculations:

Let the cost price of the article be Rs. X

⇒ X - (33/100)X = 402

⇒ 0.67X = 402

⇒ X = 402 / 0.67

⇒ X = 600

So, the cost price of the article is Rs. 600.

Now, we need to calculate the selling price at a profit of 37%. 

S.P = 600 + 0.37 × 600

S.P = 600 + 222

S.P = 822

∴The article should be sold for Rs. 822 to get a profit of 37%.

questions.question: Ritu sold two TV sets at Rs. 4,800 each gaining 20% on one and losing 20% on the other. Find out the total percentage gain or loss.
questions.questionHtml: Ritu sold two TV sets at Rs. 4,800 each gaining 20% on one and losing  20% on the other. Find out the total percentage gain or loss.
questions.solution:
Given:

Ritu sold two TV sets at Rs. 4,800 each gaining 20% on one and losing  20% on the other
Formula used:

 Profit = \(\frac{\text{selling price - cost price}}{\text{cost price}}\times100\)
Calculation:

Let the cost price of the first TV be x.

Then, \(\frac{4800-x}{x}\times100=20\)

Solving for x,

 \(x=\frac{4800}{1.2}=4000\)

Let the cost price of the second TV be y.

Then, \(\frac{4800-y}{y}\times100=-20\)

Solving for y,

 \(y=\frac{4800}{0.8}=6000\)

Therefore, the total cost price is 4000+ 6000 = Rs. 10000 and the total selling price is 4800 + 4800 = Rs. 9600 

∴ There is loss of \(\frac{10000-9600}{10000}\times100=4\%\)

Shortcut TrickWhen 2 things are sold at same price. And get x% profit on one thing and x% loss on other thing.

So the total loss would be always = (x2/100) %

So the loss percentage = (400)/100 = 4%

questions.question: The selling price of 5 articles is equal to 6 times the cost price. What is the loss/profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: The selling price of 5 articles is equal to 6 times the cost price. What is the loss/profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Given data:

Selling price of 5 articles = Cost Price of 6 articles

Calculations:

Difference in price = Cost price of 1 article.

Total articles to be sold = 5 articles

Profit % = \(1\over 5\) × 100 = 20%

 Alternate Method

Let the cost price of 1 article be "a".

⇒ cost price of 6 articles = 6a

According to the question-

Selling price of 5 articles = cost price of 6 articles

⇒ Selling price of 1 article = \(6\over 5\)a

Profit =  \(6\over 5\)a - a = \(a\over 5\)

Profit % = \({a\over 5} \over a\) × 100 = 20%

∴ The profit % is 20%.

questions.question: Sohan buys an old car for Rs. 2,47,000 and spends Rs. 18,000 on its repairs. If he sells the car for Rs. 2,78,250, his profit percentage is:
questions.questionHtml: Sohan buys an old car for Rs. 2,47,000 and spends Rs. 18,000 on its repairs. If he sells the car for Rs. 2,78,250, his profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Sohan buys car for Rs247000 and spend Rs18000 on its repairs

Sohan sells the car for Rs278250

FORMULA USED:

Profit = S.P. - C.P. 

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 

Where, S.P. = Selling price, C.P. = Cost price 

CALCULATION:

Here, we have Cost price of old car = Rs247000 

Money spent on its repairing = Rs18000 

Total C.P. = Rs.(247000 + 18000 ) = Rs265000

Now, S.P. = Rs278250 

⇒ Profit = S.P. - C.P. = ( 278250 - 265000) = Rs13,250.

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 

⇒ Profit% = (13250 /265000) × 100 = 5%.

Hence his profit percentage is 5%.

questions.solution:
Cost price of 1 kg potatoes = 25 × (100/125) ⇒ 20

questions.question: Rohan buys 5 kg of sugar for Rs 44 per kg and another 10 kg of sugar for Rs 50 per kg. What is the cost of the mixture of 15 kg of sugar for him?
questions.questionHtml:
Rohan buys 5 kg of sugar for Rs 44 per kg and another 10 kg of sugar for Rs 50 per kg.

What is the cost of the mixture of 15 kg of sugar for him?
questions.solution:
Here, quantity = 5 kg , cost per kg = Rs 44 per kg

Cost = Quantity × Cost per kg ⇒ 5 × 44 = Rs220

Again quantity = 10 kg , cost per kg = Rs50 per kg ⇒ Cost = 10 × 50 = Rs 500 

Now, cost of 15 kg = ( 220 + 500 ) = Rs720. So, cost of the mixture of 15kg sugar = 720/15 = Rs48

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought toffees at a rate of 10 for Rs. 15 and sold them at a rate of 16 for Rs. 40. Find his profit percentage. (correct to two decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought toffees at a rate of 10 for Rs. 15 and sold them at a rate of 16 for Rs. 40. Find his profit percentage. (correct to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
We know, \(\frac{CP × Quantity}{price} = \frac{SP × Quantity}{price} \) 

⇒ \(\frac{CP × 10}{15} = \frac{SP × 16}{40}\) ⇒ \(\frac{CP}{SP} = \frac{6}{10}\) 

⇒ Profit% = \(\frac{(10 - 6)}{6}\) × 100 = 66.67%

questions.question: Ravi sells a chair to Mohan at a profit 10% and Mohan sells it to Govind at profit 20%. If Govind pays Rs. 1,320 for it. Then the cost price for Ravi is:
questions.questionHtml: Ravi sells a chair to Mohan at a profit 10% and Mohan sells it to Govind at profit 20%. If Govind pays Rs. 1,320 for it. Then the cost price for Ravi is:
questions.solution:
Given

Ravi sells a chair to Mohan at a profit 10%.

Mohan sells it to Govind at profit 20%.

Govind pays Rs.1,320 for it.

Formula used

Profit ={( SP - CP) / CP} × 100

SP = Selling Price

CP = Cost Price

Calculation

Let Cost Price be Rs.x

⇒ After sells chair to Mohan at 10% CP becomes x × 110 / 100

⇒ This CP becomes SP for Govind. Govind got profit of 20% = x × (110 / 100) × 120 / 100

⇒ x (11 × 12) / 100 = 1320

⇒ x = (1320 × 100) /132

∴ CP of chair is Rs.1000

Alternate Method

Net profit = 10 + 20 + (10 × 20) / 100 = 32%

CP × (1 + 32 / 100) = 13200

CP = Rs.1000
